content: Amphotec, which is amphotericin B complexed with cholesteryl sulfate, is indicated for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis in patients who cannot tolerate effective doses of conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate due to renal impairment or unacceptable toxicity, or in cases where prior therapy with amphotericin B deoxycholate has failed. The recommended dosage for adults is 3-4 mg/kg administered intravenously once daily. The initial infusion rate is 1 mg/kg/hour, and subsequent infusions may be shortened to a 2-hour duration if the patient tolerates the treatment well. Adverse effects associated with Amphotec include chills (50-77%), fever (33-55%), hypokalemia (7-26%), elevated serum creatinine (12-21%), hyperbilirubinemia (2-19%), hypotension (9-12%), tachycardia (9-12%), nausea (8-12%), vomiting (6-11%), abnormal liver function tests (4-11%), hypertension (7-9%), hypoxia (5-9%), dyspnea (4-9%), headache (4-8%), hypomagnesemia (4-7%), increased alkaline phosphatase (3-7%), thrombocytopenia (1-7%), hyperglycemia (1-6%), and hypersensitivity reactions. Amphotec is specifically indicated for patients with progressive and potentially fatal fungal infections. It should not be used for noninvasive fungal infections, such as oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis, or esophageal candidiasis, in patients with normal neutrophil counts. Caution is advised when co-administering Amphotec with other drugs that may cause hypokalemia, such as corticosteroids or digoxin, or with other nephrotoxic medications. Amphotec is classified as Pregnancy Category B, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, it is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. The drug is supplied as a 6 mg/mL solution. To prepare the medication, gently shake the vial by hand, rotating it until all solids are dissolved. The resulting fluid may appear opalescent or clear. Do not filter the solution or use an in-line filter. Use a separate infusion line for administration; if an existing IV line is used, flush it with 5% dextrose in water (D5W) before infusion. The initial infusion rate is 1 mg/kg/hour, and subsequent infusions may be shortened to 2 hours if tolerated. Unopened vials should be stored at room temperature, protected from light and excessive heat. After reconstitution, the drug should be refrigerated at 2-8°C (36-46°F) and used within 24 hours. If further diluted with 5% dextrose, the solution should also be refrigerated and used within 24 hours. Do not freeze the solution, and discard any partially used vials.
